devesh: Saw a surge in canary where one tenant burned through surge quota and starved the shared burst lane. Neighbors p95 jumped ~3x for ~90s.

nina: Do we have a simple mitigation proposal we can ship quickly?

omar: Minimal: add a per-tenant soft-cap that returns 429 with X-Redwood-Backoff and records a deferred_admit metric. Fast to add in the admit filter.

tess: We also need a slow-leak on the bucket so tenants recover gradually, not insta-unblock. Suggest leak_rate config and a max_backoff cap.

autoscaler-bot: autoscaler: surge_event tenant=tenant-88 added=2 gpus pool=burst at=1767772260

devesh: Edgecases: SLA-weighted tenants need either small reserve or a tiered backoff. Can't treat all tenants equally.

omar: Right. Plan: tier lookup in admit path. default: soft-cap enforced. enterprise: higher threshold + slower backoff. Exempt list env var for emergency customers.

nina: Also add an emergency fast-evict flag in the drain controller for preemptions. If draining > drain_timeout we force-close idle conns and start fallback warmup.

tess: Agree but must coordinate cache warmup. If fallback cold, moving inflight leads to errors. Add warm-kv handshake and short-lived token exchange (security review).

autoscaler-bot: alert("deferred_admits_high") created by nina for canary monitor at=1767772340


devesh: Ok owners: nina will prototype admit-filter change + metrics, omar will spec tier overrides, tess take drain fast-evict patch. I'll draft a short RFC with rollout plan and kill-switch.

omar: One-liner rollout: disabled by default, enable in canary for 24h, watch deferred_admit and neighbor_p95, then region roll.

nina: I'll add SDK guidance for handling 429 + X-Redwood-Backoff (Retry-After semantics).

devesh: Great. Closing thread; link RFC when ready.
